title: California HVAC Rebates and Free HVAC Programs
h1: Are There Rebates or Free HVAC Programs in California?
description: California homeowners may qualify for HVAC rebates, utility incentives or income-qualified programs that cover repairs or new equipment. Here's how to start.
quick_answer: Yes. California has income-qualified programs that can repair or replace heating and cooling equipment at no cost, plus utility and state rebates that lower the price of efficient systems like heat pumps. Free programs are mostly for lower-income households. Rebates are open to more people but change often, so check what's available before you buy.
body:
California does have programs that help pay for HVAC work, and some cover the full cost for households that qualify. Fully free equipment is mostly limited to income-qualified programs. For everyone else, the main help comes from rebates and incentives that bring down the price of efficient equipment. Programs open and close, funding runs out and rules change, so always confirm what's current.

Are there free HVAC programs for low-income households?

Yes. These are the main ones California homeowners and renters should know about:

  • Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP): federally funded and run in California by the Department of Community Services and Development through local agencies. Besides help with energy bills, it can pay for weatherization and, in some cases, repair or replacement of unsafe or broken heating and cooling equipment.
  • Weatherization Assistance Program: also administered through local agencies, it focuses on making homes more efficient and safer, which can include furnace or AC work.
  • Energy Savings Assistance program: offered through the local gas and electric utilities for income-qualified customers. Depending on the home, it can include furnace repair or replacement and other energy upgrades at no cost.

Eligibility is based on household income and size. Your local community action agency or your utility can tell you whether you qualify and what the program covers in your area.

What rebates are available if I don't qualify for free programs?

Most homeowners won't get a free system, but rebates can make a real difference:

  • Utility rebates: utilities periodically offer rebates for efficient equipment, smart thermostats and heat pumps. Check your utility's current offers before buying.
  • State heat pump incentives: California has funded programs that pay contractors incentives for installing heat pumps, which can be passed on to homeowners. Funding comes in rounds, so availability changes.
  • Federally funded home energy rebates: California has been rolling out programs funded by federal energy legislation, with higher amounts for lower-income households.
  • Manufacturer promotions: equipment makers sometimes run seasonal rebates.

Federal tax credits for home HVAC equipment have changed under recent federal law. Check with a tax professional before counting on any federal credit.

What equipment usually qualifies for rebates?

Most incentive money goes to equipment that cuts energy use. That often means:

  • Heat pumps for heating and cooling, including ducted systems and mini-splits
  • Heat pump water heaters
  • High-efficiency furnaces and air conditioners, in some programs
  • Smart or programmable thermostats
  • Duct sealing and insulation upgrades

Heat pumps fit Southern California well. Mild coastal winters and hot inland summers suit a system that handles both heating and cooling, and state programs have put much of their incentive money toward them.

How can I spot a misleading "free HVAC" offer?

Be careful with ads or door-to-door pitches promising a free system from the government. Real assistance programs work through local agencies and utilities, and they verify income before any work happens. Be cautious if someone asks for upfront fees to release a grant, pressures you to sign the same day or asks for personal financial details before explaining the program. When in doubt, contact your utility or local agency directly.

How do I apply for HVAC rebates?

  1. Check eligibility first. Look up income-qualified programs and current rebates before you get quotes or sign anything.
  2. Read the rules. Many rebates require specific equipment ratings, a participating contractor or applying before installation.
  3. Get a proper load calculation. Rebates don't help if the system is the wrong size for your home.
  4. Keep records. Save invoices, model numbers and permits. Most programs ask for them.
  5. Submit on time. Most programs have filing deadlines, and a late application can be turned down.

faqs: Can I get a free furnace in California?

Possibly, if your household meets income limits. Programs like LIHEAP, weatherization assistance and the utility Energy Savings Assistance program can repair or replace unsafe or broken furnaces for qualifying households. Contact your local community action agency or utility to apply.
Do renters qualify for HVAC assistance programs?
Some programs serve renters, though work on the home usually needs the property owner's permission. Bill assistance through LIHEAP is often available to renters who meet income guidelines.
Are heat pump rebates still available in California?

Heat pump incentives have been offered through utilities and state programs, but funding comes and goes. Check current availability before buying, and ask your installer which programs they participate in.
Do I need a permit to get an HVAC rebate?
Many programs require proof of a permit for new HVAC equipment, and California generally requires permits for system replacements anyway. Keep a copy with your invoice.
What HVAC Systems Qualify for a Tax Credit?

The federal Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit covered qualifying heat pumps, central air conditioners, gas furnaces and some related upgrades, but under current law it doesn't apply to equipment placed in service after December 31, 2025. Systems installed in 2025 may still be claimed on that year's return. Utility and state rebate programs may still help.
